summary: Great Western Trail: New Zealand swaps cattle for sheep and wool, layering in breed diversification on top of the familiar deck-building and rondel movement of the GWT series. It's aimed at fans of the system who want a new puzzle rather than a reinvention.
praised: new sheep/wool angle keeps the formula fresh
rewards long-term deck planning like the original
criticised: very close to prior entries mechanically, limited novelty for burned-out fans
still a heavy, long game with steep onboarding
niche appeal outside existing GWT fans

interaction.kind: Same GWT-family interaction: building fees and contested track/delivery spaces
interaction.detail: As with the other Great Western Trail titles, each player runs their own rondel/deck engine, while the shared board contributes building-usage payments and a limited number of track and delivery positions to race for. A supported solo mode again signals the multiplayer layer is additive rather than central.
interaction.said: unknown — too new for an established reputation distinct from the GWT series

scoring.how_you_win: Deliver increasingly valuable sheep herds to market while building trail infrastructure; the player with the most accumulated points when the game-end trigger fires wins.
